title: Shared definitions
$comment: Frozen as schema v1 at T1's gate (PLAN.md section 7), after the contract met live data on 18 and 19 September. Uses the keyword subset implemented by tools/validate.py; an unknown keyword is an error there, never ignored. Every change since 062a245 is listed in schema/CHANGES.md with the case that forced it; a change after the freeze needs a new schema_version and a row there.

number.description: An exact number: a decimal or p/q. One grammar across every implementation (fixtures/vectors/numbers.json).

code.description: A reason code or a check name.

reference.description: source:series:statistic[:window], never free text. 'synthetic' for fixtures. Up to FOUR segments after the source: PLAN section 6 names hl:perp:BTC:mark-twap:60s and hl:perp:BTC:trade-twap:90s, where the series is itself two parts and the window is a fourth. The pattern allowed three, so it refused two of the four ids that document lists -- undetected because no fixture used a windowed hl: id.

domain.description: Closed: both ends belong to it.

pays_on.description: Where an indicator pays. A missing bound is unbounded; a present bound always states who owns it.

source.description: The retained response the price is read from, so a checker can read it again.

clause.description: P&L >= min_pnl on the interval; the whole domain when 'on' is absent.

cost.description: What a leg cost. 'fixed' is a hypothetical per-unit price, multiplied by size. 'walked' is the exact total paid to acquire the whole size along one named path, carrying the book it was walked on. A total rather than a per-unit price because the total is what walking the book measures: a walk over several levels has no single price, and its average is a derived quantity that is usually a repeating decimal (1409 contracts at 645.76904 averages 8072113/17612500). Both forms are exact under the number grammar; the total is the one that was observed.

levels.description: The displayed asks the walk saw, in book order, as exact [price, size] pairs. The total above is what this size cost; these are what any other size would cost, so the size window is derived from the same bytes as the price and needs no second look at the book.

witness.description: A price alone is a counterexample only when no leg was bounded; otherwise it carries the adverse state of each reduced leg.

capture.description: How the snapshots in this result were captured, as stated by whatever captured them. A pure evaluator cannot re-derive this: the contexts response carries no venue timestamp (EVIDENCE section 4), so the spread between a book's venue clock and the baseline's retrieval is measurable only at capture time. It is therefore an assertion, recorded so a reader can see it and a stale or wide capture is visible, not a fact the kernel establishes. `max_skew_ms` is the bound the capturer refused above.

skew_ms.description: The worst observed |book venue time - local retrieval time| across the snapshots in this result, in whole milliseconds.

max_skew_ms.description: The bound the capturer enforced. A capture above it is refused, never recorded.

integer_text.description: A whole number as a string. Milliseconds are counted, never measured, so they carry no fraction.

order_envelope.description: The order the cost bound assumes. A depth-priced cost is the cost of ONE order and of no other: walking asks for 924 contracts bounds the cost only if the order that runs is a buy of exactly 924 contracts, priced no worse than the highest level the walk touched, and cancelled rather than rested. Any other order has a different cost and the result says nothing about it. `limit_price` is the price of the highest level the walk touched, `max_cost` the walked total, and `input_digest` the result this envelope belongs to, so an envelope cannot be carried to a different answer.

coin.description: The venue's own id for the instrument, as discovered.

side.description: Buy only. Acquiring protection is the only side a cost bound from the ask side can bound.

limit_price.description: The price of the HIGHEST level the walk touched. A fill at any price the book displayed for this size is at or below it, so the order cannot cost more than the bound.

time_in_force.description: Ioc only. A resting order outlives the book that priced it, so the bound would stop being about the evidence.
